flawed_step: Step 3: after writing P(S|T) = P(C|T)P(S|T,C) + P(not-C|T)P(S|T,not-C) and P(S|not-T) = P(C|not-T)P(S|not-T,C) + P(not-C|not-T)P(S|not-T,not-C), concluding P(S|T) > P(S|not-T) from the termwise inequalities. The two averages use different weights (P(C|T) need not equal P(C|not-T)), so the inequality is not preserved (Simpson's paradox).
counterexample: Uniform space of 700 individuals. C: T has 81/87 successes (0.931), not-T has 234/270 (0.867). not-C: T has 192/263 (0.730), not-T has 55/80 (0.6875). Overall: P(S|T)=273/350=0.78 < P(S|not-T)=289/350≈0.826.
assessment_summary: Simpson's paradox. The overall rates are weighted averages of the stratum rates, but the weights differ between T and not-T, so the treatment can win in every stratum and still lose overall. The kidney-stone data is a concrete counterexample in which all four cells have positive probability.
